entities.summary:
Huai of Xia: Eighth King of the Semi-Legendary Xia Dynasty of Ancient China

Born in an unknown year, Huai's reign is shrouded in mystery due to varying accounts of its duration, with some sources estimating 26 years and others 44. As the eighth king of the Xia dynasty, he played a crucial role in the development of Ancient Chinese history.

During his rule, Huai oversaw significant events that shaped the course of Chinese civilization. He was responsible for the construction of several major cities, including the capital city of Yi, and implemented policies aimed at strengthening the economy and military. Despite the uncertainty surrounding his reign, Huai's legacy has left a lasting impact on the region.

In 2100 BCE, Huai died, marking the end of an era in Ancient Chinese history. His death paved the way for the transition to the Shang dynasty, one of China's earliest historical dynasties.
